claims.quote: Renderers must scale content into the space represented by the Canvas, and should follow any timeMode value provided for time-based media.
claims.supports: scaling mandated; no fit algorithm anywhere in stable 3.0 ('scaled' absent as exact string)

claims.quote: A Canvas may be treated as a content resource for the purposes of annotating it on to other Canvases.
claims.supports: Canvas-as-body permitted in STABLE 3.0 (re-confirms E16)

claims.claim: width/height convey an aspect ratio for the space in which content resources are located; for Canvases the value does not have a unit
claims.supports: Canvas = unit-less coordinate space / frame of reference

claims.claim: SVG / image/svg+xml appears ZERO times in the entire document; 'scaled' zero times; no z-order/paint-order semantics
claims.supports: P1 has no external anchor; z-order is not normative

claims.claim: timeMode value 'scale' defines temporal fitting (duration of content resource fitted to Canvas portion)
claims.supports: contrast: temporal fit parameterized, spatial fit not

claims.quote: The interval is half-open: the begin time is considered part of the interval whereas the end time is considered to be the first time point that is not part of the interval.
claims.supports: lab half-open [start,end) convention is the NORMATIVE reading

claims.quote: If percent is used, x and width are interpreted as a percentage of the width of the original media, and y and height are interpreted as a percentage of the original height.
claims.supports: percent axis-split as lab implemented (open question #7)

claims.claim: pixel coordinates are interpreted after taking into account the resource's dimensions, aspect ratio, clean aperture, resolution
claims.supports: selector-side coordinates are RESOURCE-intrinsic

claims.claim: (non-normative) pixel coords intended identical to HTML5 intrinsic dimensions; HTML rendering clients expected to implement cropping as default; highlight-vs-crop out of scope
claims.supports: tension with IIIF placement practice recorded as contradiction #3

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model, W3C Recommendation

claims.supports: normative WA→Media Fragments chain for selector coordinate semantics

claims.quote: The dimensions of the SVG shape or canvas MUST be relative to the dimensions of the Source resource, such that scaling the shape's size to the full size of the image correctly describes the desired area.
claims.supports: existing normative SVG↔source mapping rule — SELECTION-side, proportional/stretch-style, NO aspect-ratio logic; contrast with P2's meet model recorded

claims.quote: Implementers SHOULD use only commonly supported features of SVG that directly contribute to describing a region... It is NOT RECOMMENDED to include style information within the SVG element, nor Javascript, animation, text...
claims.supports: community accepts feature-restricted SVG inside annotations; adjacent precedent for sanitizer/text-determinism positions

claims.claim: the word 'coordinate(s)' appears nowhere in the document; no mismatch behavior defined beyond the proportional sentence
claims.supports: WA gives no general coordinate-system framework beyond selectors

sources.title: IIIF Cookbook: Image and Canvas with Differing Dimensions

claims.quote: This recipe demonstrates the importance of thinking about a Canvas as a coordinate space, not as absolute pixel or display dimensions.
claims.supports: Canvas-as-coordinate-space framing

claims.quote: Finally, if the image dimensions are larger than the Canvas, the image will be scaled to fit the Canvas.
claims.supports: 'scaled to fit' used without algorithm

claims.quote: The aspect ratio should be consistent between your source image and Canvas. Otherwise, you'll see unpredictable stretching and/or distorting.
claims.supports: INDEPENDENT community endorsement of same-aspect discipline (= lab P5a); admits ecosystem unpredictability on mismatch

sources.title: IIIF Cookbook: Composition from Multiple Images

claims.quote: The resource are assembled upwards on the canvas in the order they are provided in the Manifest. This works like Z-index in CSS. ... The presentation of images is upwards in a z-index from the first painting annotation encountered
claims.supports: z-order convention first=bottom (matches P4); COMMUNITY rank only

claims.quote: Note: Currently, Mirador 3 only partially supports the layering of multiple images on a single Canvas... Mirador 3 does this in reverse.
claims.supports: viewer divergence on identical construction documented BY IIIF (Q8 yes)

claims.claim: Fragment Selector used to position a smaller image into a region of the Canvas
claims.supports: region-targeted placement practice exists in cookbook

sources.title: IIIF Cookbook: Multiple Choice of Images in a Single View

claims.quote: While previous iterations of Mirador processed the images upwards from the first painting annotation, Mirador 3 does this in reverse. This means that the first image in the 'choice' body sits at the top of the 'stack' in Mirador 3 rather than at the bottom.
claims.supports: second documentation of Mirador reversal

sources.title: IIIF Cookbook: Rendering Multiple Media Types on a Time-Based Canvas

claims.quote: The simultaneously visible resources are listed in the Manifest from the foreground to the background. The timer video comes first in the Manifest, as the only currently capable viewer places resources on the Canvas so that the first resource is the most foregrounded.
claims.supports: OPPOSITE stacking direction attributed to the one capable AV viewer — recipes contradict each other; z-order cannot be cited as settled practice
temporal precision caveat relevant to temporal annotations
